name: Panch Phoron Tarkari
ingredients: Mixed seasonal vegetables (pumpkin, potato, eggplant, beans, raw banana)
Panch Phoron (equal parts of fennel seeds, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, nigella seeds, and cumin seeds)
instructions: 1. Chop all vegetables into uniform medium-sized cubes.
2. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until it reaches a smoking point.
3. Add the Panch Phoron seeds and dried red chilies to the oil until they crackle and release an aroma.
4. Add the ginger and green chilies, sautéing briefly.
5. Add the harder vegetables like potatoes and raw bananas first, sautéing for a few minutes.
6. Add the softer vegetables, turmeric powder, and salt, mixing well.
7. Add a small amount of water, cover, and simmer until all vegetables are tender.
8. Adjust consistency and serve warm with steamed rice.
description: Panch Phoron Tarkari is a quintessential Bengali-influenced dish staple in Tripuri households. It highlights the simplicity of North-East Indian cooking, relying on the distinct aromatic profile of the five-seed spice blend to provide flavor without the use of heavy onion-garlic masalas.
